1.q: הַ⁠דָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵ⁠אֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה
1.note: See how you translated this expression in [7:1](ta:07).
The words **Jehoiakim** and **Josiah** are the names of men.

2.note: Here, **house** represents “family.” Yahweh is referring to the descendants of a man named Rechab. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verses 3, 5, and 18. Alternate translation: [where the families of the Rechabites live]
See how you translated the similar expression in 17:26. This also occurs in verse 4.

3.q: אֶת יַאֲזַנְיָ֤ה בֶֽן יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן חֲבַצִּנְיָ֔ה
3.note: The words **Jaazaniah**, **Jeremiah**, and **Habazziniah** are the names of men. This man named Jeremiah is not the prophet Jeremiah.

4.note: The words **Hanan** and **Igdaliah** are the names of men.

Jeremiah is using **the man of God** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the prophet.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the prophet of God]
The words **Maaseiah** and **Shallum** are the names of men.

Jeremiah is using **the keeper of the threshold** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the official who guarded the entrance of the temple.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the official who guarded the temple entrance]

6.q: יוֹנָדָ֨ב בֶּן רֵכָ֜ב אָבִ֗י⁠נוּ צִוָּ֤ה עָלֵ֨י⁠נוּ֙ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר לֹ֧א תִשְׁתּוּ יַ֛יִן אַתֶּ֥ם וּ⁠בְנֵי⁠כֶ֖ם עַד עוֹלָֽם
6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us that neither we nor our sons should ever drink wine]
The words **Jonadab** and **Rechab** are the names of men. This also occurs in verse 19.

Here, **our father** represents “our ancestor.” Jonadab was not the father of these men but an ancestor who lived many generations before them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [our forefather]

Jonadab is using **forever** as a common expression of the culture to mean “at any time, for all generations.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [ever, in any generation]

7.note: Jonadab used **all your days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “always” or “for your entire lives.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all your lives]
See how you translated this expression in 25:26.

The implication is that the Rechabites would be living in the land as foreigners who did not own any of it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [where you are residing as foreigners who own no land]

8.note: The Rechabites are using **we have listened to the voice of Jonadab** as a common expression of the culture to mean “we have obeyed Jonadab.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And we have obeyed Jonadab]

9.note: Here, **seed** represents “crops” that grow from seeds that are planted. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [or harvest]

11.q: בַּ⁠עֲל֨וֹת נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֮ אֶל הָ⁠אָרֶץ֒
11.note: The implication is that Nebuchadnezzar **came up against the land** with his army in order to attack it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up with his army to attack the land]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that we urged one another to go to Jerusalem]

11.q: מִ⁠פְּנֵי֙ חֵ֣יל הַ⁠כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּ⁠מִ⁠פְּנֵ֖י חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֑ם
11.note: The Rechabites are using **from before the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to escape from the presence of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to flee from the army of the Chaldeans and from the army of Aram]
The word **Chaldeans** is the name of a people group. It is another name for the Babylonians.

12.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 28:12.

Jeremiah is speaking about himself in the third person, even though he has been telling this account in the first person. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use the first person form. Alternate translation: [to me]

13.note: See how you translated this expression in 4:3.

13.q: הֲ⁠ל֨וֹא תִקְח֥וּ מוּסָ֛ר לִ⁠שְׁמֹ֥עַ אֶל דְּבָרַ֖⁠י
13.note: Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis, to rebuke the people of Judah and Jerusalem for refusing to obey him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should receive correction and listen to my words!]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **correction**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [it when I correct you and learn]
See how you translated the similar expression in 31:23.

14.q: הוּקַ֡ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוֹנָדָ֣ב בֶּן־רֵ֠כָב אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה אֶת־בָּנָ֜י⁠ו לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֣י שְׁתֽוֹת־יַ֗יִן
14.note: The expression **have been carried out** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, Yahweh implies that the descendants of Jonadab did it. Alternate translation: [The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have carried out the words that he commanded them, to not drink wine]
Yahweh is speaking as if the later generations of Rechabites were actually the **sons** of Jonadab. Alternate translation: [his descendants]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I have spoken** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize the contrast between himself, who has spoken to the people again and again, and Jonadab, who only commanded his sons once. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [But I myself have spoken to you]
See how you translated **rising early and speaking** in 7:13.
Yahweh is speaking as if the people of the Rechabite clan were actually Jonadab’s **sons**. Alternate translation: [his descendants]

15.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 29:19.
See how you translated this phrase in 25:4.
See how you translated the similar expression in 18:11.
See how you translated this phrase in 23:22.

Here the prophets are speaking as if serving other gods were to **walk after** them, the way a follower walks behind a leader. It means that the people should not worship **other gods** or practice the false religion of that god. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not devote yourselves to other gods]
See how you translated this expression in 7:24.

16.note: Jeremiah is speaking as if the people of the clan of the Rechabites were actually the **sons** of Jonadab. See how you translated “” in 35:14 where it is used with the same meaning. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Jonadab]
See how you translated the names **Jonadab** and **Rechab** in 35:6.
See how you translated the word “father” in 35:6 where it is used with the same meaning.

17.q: דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֲלֵי⁠הֶם֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֔עוּ וָ⁠אֶקְרָ֥א לָ⁠הֶ֖ם וְ⁠לֹ֥א עָנֽוּ
17.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [I spoke to them again and again, but they refused to respond to me]

18.note: Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So the **house of the Rechabites** means all the people descended from Rechab. Alternate translation: [And to the descendants of Rechab]

18.q: שְׁמַעְתֶּ֔ם עַל־מִצְוַ֖ת יְהוֹנָדָ֣ב אֲבִי⁠כֶ֑ם וַֽ⁠תִּשְׁמְרוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתָ֔י⁠ו וַֽ⁠תַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כְּ⁠כֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖ה אֶתְ⁠כֶֽם
18.note: These three clauses mean basically the same thing. The second and third emphasize the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [you have carefully obeyed everything that Jonadab your father commanded you]

19.q: לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֨ת אִ֜ישׁ לְ⁠יוֹנָדָ֧ב בֶּן רֵכָ֛ב
19.note: Yahweh is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [Jonadab son of Rechab will certainly have a man]

The expression **will not be cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who would do the action, Yahweh implies that he himself would do it. Alternate translation: [will not fail]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:10.
See how you translated the this expression in 31:36.
